a: when all the evil and the wicked are taken away
p: The Greek names "enemies"; the Ge'ez names the evil and the wicked.

readings.orig: ለአሰስሎ ኲሉ እኩያን ወረሲዓን (läʾäsäslo kʷilu ʾəkuyan wäräsiʿan)
readings.en: to remove all the evil and the godless
readings.plain: when all the evil and the wicked are taken away

readings.orig: ἐξᾶραι πάντας τοὺς ἐχθρούς, ⟨καὶ σωθήσονται δίκαιοι⟩ (exarai pantas tous echthrous, kai sōthēsontai dikaioi)
readings.en: to remove all the enemies, and the righteous will be saved
readings.plain: when all the enemies are taken away, and the righteous will be saved

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez. The two agree on the main point, the removal of the wicked; "enemies" may be a Greek translator's word for the same Aramaic. The Greek manuscript also adds "and the righteous will be saved," which has no Ethiopic parallel.

a: on all the righteous too
p: Only the Ge'ez has these words.

readings.orig: ወላዕለ ጻድቃን ኲሎሙ (wälaʿlä ṣadqan kʷilomu)
readings.en: and upon all the righteous
readings.plain: on all the righteous too

readings.en: (no words here)

why: The Plain English Translation keeps the Ge'ez, the base text, but marks the words because the Greek lacks them. They may have come in from 1:8, which begins with the righteous.

a: you will make your names an everlasting curse
p: The Greek says "names"; the Ge'ez says "peace."

readings.orig: τότε ἔσται τὰ ὀνόματα ὑμῶν εἰς κατάραν αἰώνιον (tote estai ta onomata hymōn eis kataran aiōnion)
readings.en: then your names will be for an everlasting curse
readings.plain: you will make your names an everlasting curse

readings.orig: ትሁቡ ሰላመ ዚአክሙ በርግመት ዘለዓለም (təhubu sälamä ziʾäkmu bärgəmät zäläʿaläm)
readings.en: you will give your peace as an everlasting curse
readings.plain: you will give your peace as an everlasting curse

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek, which matches Isaiah 65:15 ("you will leave your name as a curse for my chosen"), the passage 5:6–9 is built on. How the Ge'ez "peace" arose is not known; a copying slip is only a guess.

a: They came down in the days of Jared on the top of Mount Hermon
t: "In the days of Jared," or "on Ardis"?
p: Syncellus's Greek has "in the days of Jared"; the Ge'ez has a place name, Ardis.

readings.w: Greek quoted by George Syncellus, about AD 810
readings.orig: οἱ καταβάντες ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἰάρεδ εἰς τὴν κορυφὴν τοῦ Ἑρμονιεὶμ ὄρους (hoi katabantes en tais hēmerais Iared eis tēn koryphēn tou Hermonieim orous)
readings.en: who came down in the days of Jared to the top of Mount Hermon
readings.plain: They came down in the days of Jared on the top of Mount Hermon

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible reads the same, with small spelling differences
readings.orig: ወወረዱ ውስተ አርዲስ ዝውእቱ ድማሑ ለደብረ አርሞን (wäwärädu wəstä ʾärdis zəwʾətu dəmaḥu lädäbrä ʾärmon)
readings.en: and they came down on Ardis, which is the summit of Mount Hermon
readings.plain: They came down on Ardis, which is the top of Mount Hermon

readings.en: (this verse is missing; the copyist skipped from 6:5 to 6:7)

why: The Plain English Translation follows Syncellus. Charles explained the Ge'ez "Ardis" as a garbled form of the Greek Iared, so that the time ("in the days of Jared") turned into a place name. Jubilees 4:15 and 1 Enoch 106:13 also place the angels' descent in the days of Jared, whose name sounds like "go down." The Aramaic fragments of this verse are too damaged to settle the wording.

a: each of them three thousand cubits tall
t: Three thousand cubits, and three kinds of giants
p: The Ge'ez and the Gizeh Greek give the height; Syncellus gives three generations instead.

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible reads the same, with small spelling differences
readings.orig: ወቆሞሙ በበ ፴፻ በእመት (wäqomomu bäbä [3000] bäʾmät)
readings.en: and their height was three thousand cubits each
readings.plain: each of them three thousand cubits tall

readings.orig: ἐτέκοσαν γίγαντας μεγάλους ἐκ πηχῶν τρισχιλίων (etekosan gigantas megalous ek pēchōn trischiliōn)
readings.en: they bore great giants of three thousand cubits
readings.plain: each of them three thousand cubits tall

readings.w: Greek quoted by George Syncellus, about AD 810
readings.orig: καὶ ἔτεκον αὐτοῖς γένη τρία· πρῶτον γίγαντας μεγάλους. οἱ δὲ γίγαντες ἐτέκνωσαν Ναφηλείμ, καὶ τοῖς Ναφηλεὶμ ἐγεννήθησαν Ἐλιούδ (kai etekon autois genē tria; prōton gigantas megalous. hoi de gigantes eteknōsan Naphēleim, kai tois Naphēleim egennēthēsan Elioud)
readings.en: and they bore to them three kinds: first great giants; the giants fathered Nephilim, and to the Nephilim were born Elioud
readings.plain: and they bore three kinds: first huge giants; the giants fathered the Nephilim, and the Nephilim fathered the Elioud

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez and the Gizeh Greek, which agree. Dillmann writes the number in figures and the EOTC text in words ("thirty hundred"). Syncellus has no height but three generations; the Dream Visions also know three kinds of giant offspring (see 86:4).

a: He showed them the metals and how to work them
p: The Greek has "metals"; the Ge'ez seems to have misread the same Greek letters.

readings.orig: καὶ ὑπέδειξεν αὐτοῖς τὰ μέταλλα καὶ τὴν ἐργασίαν αὐτῶν (kai hypedeixen autois ta metalla kai tēn ergasian autōn)
readings.en: and he showed them the metals and their working
readings.plain: He showed them the metals and how to work them

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible reads the same, with small spelling differences
readings.orig: ወአርአዮሙ ዘእምድኅሬሆሙ ወምግባረሆሙ (wäʾärʾäyomu zäʾmədḫərehomu wämgəbarähomu)
readings.en: and he showed them what is after them and their working
readings.plain: He showed them what comes after them and how to work it

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. "What is after them" in the Ge'ez matches Greek met' auta, "after them," which a translator could read for metalla, "metals." The next words, "and their working," only make sense with metals.

a: Semyaza taught all who cast spells and cut roots
p: The Greek names Semyaza as the teacher of spells; the Ge'ez has Amezarak.

readings.orig: Σεμιαζᾶς ἐδίδαξεν ἐπαοιδὰς καὶ ῥιζοτομίας (Semiazas edidaxen epaoidas kai rhizotomias)
readings.en: Semiazas taught spells and root-cuttings
readings.plain: Semyaza taught all who cast spells and cut roots

readings.orig: አሜዛራክ መሀረ ኲሎ መሳብዕያነ ወመታርያነ ሥርዋት (ʾämezarak mähärä kʷilo mäsabʿəyanä wämätaryanä śərwat)
readings.en: Amezarak taught all the enchanters and root-cutters
readings.plain: Amezarak taught all who cast spells and cut roots

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek, since Semyaza is the Watchers' leader (6:3) and his name appears here in both the Gizeh and Syncellus copies. "Amezarak" is probably a worn-down form of the same name. The other names in this verse are spelled differently in every witness; the Plain English Translation uses the forms of the Ge'ez for those.

a: Michael, Uriel, Raphael and Gabriel
p: The Greek names Uriel; the Ge'ez has two other names, and the Aramaic seems to have Sariel.

readings.orig: Μιχαὴλ καὶ Οὐριὴλ καὶ Ῥαφαὴλ καὶ Γαβριή(λ) (Michaēl kai Ouriēl kai Rhaphaēl kai Gabriēl)
readings.en: Michael and Uriel and Raphael and Gabriel
readings.plain: Michael, Uriel, Raphael and Gabriel

readings.orig: ሚካኤል ወገብርኤል ወሱርያን ወኡርያን (mikaʾel wägäbrəʾel wäsuryan wäʾuryan)
readings.en: Michael and Gabriel and Suryan and Uryan
readings.plain: Michael, Gabriel, Suryan and Uryan

readings.w: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church printed text (EOTC)
readings.orig: ሚካኤል ወገብርኤል ወሱሩያል ወኡርያል (mikaʾel wägäbrəʾel wäsuruyal wäʾuryal)
readings.en: Michael and Gabriel and Suruyal and Uryal
readings.plain: Michael, Gabriel, Suruyal and Uryal

readings.en: Michael, Sariel, Raphael and Gabriel (as Milik reads and restores the damaged lines; not checked here against his plates)
readings.plain: Michael, Sariel, Raphael and Gabriel

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Gizeh Greek, which Syncellus's Greek supports. The Ge'ez "Suryan/Suruyal" may be a form of Sariel and "Uryan/Uryal" of Uriel, so the Ethiopic may keep traces of both names in a different order. Milik's reading of the Aramaic is widely cited, but the letters are damaged. If Sariel is right, it also explains the strange names in 10:1.

a: He sent Uriel to the son of Lamech
p: Syncellus's Greek names Uriel; the Gizeh Greek and the Ge'ez have strange names.

readings.w: Greek quoted by George Syncellus, about AD 810
readings.orig: καὶ ἔπεμψε τὸν Οὐριὴλ πρὸς τὸν υἱὸν Λάμεχ (kai epempse ton Ouriēl pros ton huion Lamech)
readings.en: and he sent Uriel to the son of Lamech
readings.plain: He sent Uriel to the son of Lamech

readings.orig: καὶ ἔπεμψεν Ἰστραὴλ πρὸς τὸν υἱὸν Λέμεχ (kai epempsen Istraēl pros ton huion Lemech)
readings.en: and he sent Istrael to the son of Lemech
readings.plain: He sent Istrael to the son of Lamech

readings.orig: ወፈነዎ ለአርስየላልዩር ኀበ ወልደ ላሜክ (wäfänäwo läʾärsəyälalyur ḫäbä wäldä lamek)
readings.en: and he sent Arsyalalyur to the son of Lamech
readings.plain: He sent Arsyalalyur to the son of Lamech

why: The Plain English Translation follows Syncellus, whose Uriel matches the four archangels of 9:1 in the Greek. But many scholars, including Milik and Nickelsburg, explain both strange names, Gizeh "Istrael" and Ge'ez "Arsyalalyur," as corruptions of Sariel, the name the Aramaic seems to have among the four in 9:1. On that view Sariel was the angel sent to Noah, and "Uriel" in Syncellus and in the Greek of 9:1 is a later normalization to the better-known name. The Plain English Translation keeps Uriel because it is the only witness that names an angel clearly, and marks the doubt here.

a: the secret things the Watchers told and taught their sons
p: The three witnesses have three different verbs.

readings.w: Greek quoted by George Syncellus, about AD 810
readings.orig: ἐν τῷ μυστηρίῳ ὃ εἶπον οἱ ἐγρήγοροι καὶ ἐδίδαξαν τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτῶν (en tō mystēriō ho eipon hoi egrēgoroi kai edidaxan tous huious autōn)
readings.en: by the mystery which the Watchers told and taught their sons
readings.plain: the secret things the Watchers told and taught their sons

readings.orig: ἐν τῷ μυστηρίῳ ὅλῳ ᾧ ἐπέτασαν οἱ ἐγρήγοροι (en tō mystēriō holō hō epetasan hoi egrēgoroi)
readings.en: by the whole mystery which the Watchers spread out
readings.plain: the secret things the Watchers spread and taught their sons

readings.orig: በምሥጢረ ኲሉ ዘቀተሉ ትጉሃን ወመሀሩ ለውሉዶሙ (bämśəṭirä kʷilu zäqätälu təguhan wämähäru läwludomu)
readings.en: by the secret of all that the Watchers killed and taught their sons
readings.plain: the secret things the Watchers killed and taught their sons

why: The Plain English Translation follows Syncellus, the only reading that makes clear sense. The Gizeh verb epetasan, "spread out," may be a slip for a similar Greek word; the Ge'ez "killed" fits a Greek copy that read epataxan, "struck," for the same letters.

a: Go and make this known to Semyaza
p: Syncellus says "bind Semyaza." The Gizeh Greek and the Ge'ez say "make known."

readings.orig: አይድዕ ለስምያዛ (ʾäydəʿ läsməyaza)
readings.en: make known to Semyaza
readings.plain: Go and make this known to Semyaza

readings.orig: Πορεύου καὶ δήλωσον Σεμιαζᾷ (Poreuou kai dēlōson Semiaza)
readings.en: Go and make known to Semiazas
readings.plain: Go and make this known to Semyaza

readings.w: Greek quoted by George Syncellus, about AD 810
readings.orig: πορεύου Μιχαήλ, δῆσον Σεμιαζᾶν (poreuou Michaēl, dēson Semiazan)
readings.en: Go, Michael, bind Semiazas
readings.plain: Go and bind Semyaza

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez and the Gizeh Greek. Greek dēlōson, "make known," and dēson, "bind," differ by two letters. Syncellus's "bind" matches 10:4 and 10:12, and some scholars prefer it, but two of the three witnesses agree on "make known." The Ge'ez has no "go"; the Plain English Translation takes it from both Greek copies.

a: Because they delight in their children
t: "Because they delight" or "they will not delight"?
p: Dillmann's Ge'ez has a negative. The EOTC text and the Greek do not.

readings.w: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church printed text (EOTC)
readings.orig: እስመ ይትፌሥሑ በውሉዶሙ (ʾəsmä yətfeśḥu bäwludomu)
readings.en: because they rejoice in their children
readings.plain: Because they delight in their children

readings.w: Greek, Gizeh (Akhmim) manuscript, 6th century (Charles 1893), at the end of 12:5
readings.orig: καὶ περὶ ὧν χαίρουσιν τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῶν (kai peri hōn chairousin tōn huiōn autōn)
readings.en: and concerning their sons in whom they rejoice
readings.plain: Because they delight in their children

readings.orig: እስመ ኢይትፌሥሑ በውሉዶሙ (ʾəsmä ʾiytəfeśḥu bäwludomu)
readings.en: for they will not rejoice in their children
readings.plain: They will not delight in their children

why: The Plain English Translation follows the EOTC text and the Greek: the Watchers' joy in their sons is what makes the sons' deaths a punishment (10:12; 14:6). Dillmann's negative reads well too ("they will have no joy in their children"), so the two say nearly the same thing.

a: but he had no need of holy counsel
t: No need of counsel, or "his word is a deed"?
p: The Greek has "every word of his is a deed" where the Ge'ez speaks of counsel.

readings.orig: ወውእቱሰ ኢይፈቅድ ምክረ ቅድስተ (wäwʾətusä ʾiyfäqd məkrä qədsətä)
readings.en: but he needs no holy counsel
readings.plain: but he had no need of holy counsel

readings.orig: καὶ πᾶς λόγος αὐτοῦ ἔργον (kai pas logos autou ergon)
readings.en: and every word of his is a deed
readings.plain: and every word of his is a deed

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez, the base text. The Greek line, "every word of his is a deed," is a fine phrase (compare Psalm 33:9) and makes the same point, that God needs no advisers; the two may be different translations of one Aramaic line.

a: Because they were created from above
p: The Greek says the giants came from human beings.

readings.orig: እስመ እመልዕልት ተፈጥሩ (ʾəsmä ʾəmälʿəlt täfäṭru)
readings.en: because they were created from above
readings.plain: Because they were created from above

readings.orig: διότι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐγένοντο (dioti apo tōn anthrōpōn egenonto)
readings.en: because they came into being from human beings
readings.plain: Because they came into being from human beings

readings.w: Greek quoted by George Syncellus, about AD 810
readings.orig: διότι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἐγένοντο (dioti apo tōn anthrōpōn egenonto)
readings.en: because they came into being from human beings
readings.plain: Because they came into being from human beings

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez, although both Greek witnesses read "from human beings", which fits what follows: "their beginning … was from the holy Watchers." The Greek is also true of the giants, whose mothers were human, and may explain why the spirits rise against humans "because they came out of them" (15:12).

a: they do not thirst
p: The Ge'ez says the spirits do not thirst; the Greek says they do.

readings.orig: ወኢይጸምዑ (wäʾiyṣämʿu)
readings.en: and they do not thirst
readings.plain: they do not thirst

readings.orig: καὶ διψῶντα (kai dipsōnta)
readings.en: and thirsting
readings.plain: they are thirsty

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez, the base text. The Greek's "eating nothing … and thirsting" may be older: spirits without bodies who still crave (compare Luke 11:24). Charles followed the Greek.

a: There the heavens come to an end
p: The Greek says the heavens end there; the Ge'ez says the waters gather.

readings.orig: ἐκεῖ συντελεσθήσονται οἱ οὐρανοί (ekei syntelesthēsontai hoi ouranoi)
readings.en: there the heavens will be completed
readings.plain: There the heavens come to an end

readings.orig: ይትጋብኡ ማያት (yətgabʾu mayat)
readings.en: there the waters gather
readings.plain: There the waters gather

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. Ge'ez mayat, "waters," and sämayat, "heavens," differ by one syllable, and the next verses (18:12, 14) describe the edge of the sky.

a: ten thousand years
t: "Ten thousand years," or "the year of mystery"?
p: The Greek gives a number; the Ge'ez has "in the year of mystery."

readings.orig: ἐνιαυτῶν μυρίων (eniautōn myriōn)
readings.en: of ten thousand years
readings.plain: ten thousand years

readings.orig: በዓመተ ምሥጢር (bäʿamätä məśṭir)
readings.en: in the year of mystery
readings.plain: in the year of mystery

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek, which 21:6 supports ("until ten thousand … are completed"). The Ge'ez phrase probably comes from a misreading of the Greek number.

a: who led the angels of heaven astray
p: The Greek calls the women "wives of the angels who went astray."

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible agrees, but lacks "of heaven"
readings.orig: አስሒቶን መላእክተ ሰማይ (ʾäsḥiton mälaʾkətä sämay)
readings.en: who led astray the angels of heaven
readings.plain: who led the angels of heaven astray

readings.orig: αἱ γυναῖκες αὐτῶν, τῶν παραβάντων ἀγγέλων (hai gynaikes autōn, tōn parabantōn angelōn)
readings.en: their wives, of the angels who went astray
readings.plain: the wives of the angels who went astray

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez, the base text, though the Greek may be older: chapters 6–7 put the blame on the angels. The note on this verse discusses the difference.

a: will become sirens
p: The Greek says sirens. The Ge'ez says "peaceful ones."

readings.orig: εἰς σειρῆνας γενήσονται (eis seirēnas genēsontai)
readings.en: they will become sirens
readings.plain: will become sirens

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible agrees, with a small spelling difference
readings.orig: ከመ ሰላማውያን ይከውና (kämä sälamawyan yəkäwna)
readings.en: they will become like peaceful ones
readings.plain: will become like peaceful ones

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. A Greek copy that read eirēnaiai, "peaceful," for seirēnes, "sirens," explains the Ge'ez. "Peaceful" makes little sense in a verse about punishment.

a: who is over the world and over Tartarus
p: The Greek gives Uriel the world and Tartarus. The Ge'ez says thunder and trembling.

readings.orig: ὁ ἐπὶ τοῦ κόσμου καὶ τοῦ ταρτάρου (ho epi tou kosmou kai tou tartarou)
readings.en: who is over the world and over Tartarus
readings.plain: who is over the world and over Tartarus

readings.orig: እስመ ዘረዓም ወዘረዓድ (ʾəsmä zäräʿam wäzäräʿad)
readings.en: for he is (over) thunder and trembling
readings.plain: who is over thunder and trembling

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek, found in both Gizeh copies. Uriel guides Enoch to the prisons of the stars and angels (19:1; 21:5–10), which fits Tartarus. How the Ge'ez reading arose is not clear; it may come from a damaged Greek copy.

a: Saraqael
p: The Greek has Sariel.

readings.orig: ሰረቃኤል (säräqaʾel)
readings.en: Saraqael
readings.plain: Saraqael

readings.orig: Σαριήλ (Sariēl)
readings.en: Sariel
readings.plain: Sariel

why: The Plain English Translation keeps the Ge'ez name. The Greek Sariel is probably the older form, and it agrees with the Aramaic of 9:1 as Milik read it.

a: Remiel, one of the holy angels, whom God has put in charge of those who rise.
p: Only the second Greek copy has this verse. The Ge'ez lists six angels.

readings.orig: Ῥεμειὴλ (ὁ) εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων ὃν ἔταξεν ὁ θεὸς ἐπὶ τῶν ἀνισταμένων (Rhemeiēl ho heis tōn hagiōn angelōn hon etaxen ho theos epi tōn anistamenōn)
readings.en: Remiel, one of the holy angels, whom God set over those who rise
readings.plain: Remiel, one of the holy angels, whom God has put in charge of those who rise.

readings.en: (no verse here; the list ends with Gabriel)

why: The Plain English Translation includes the verse from the Greek. The second Gizeh copy has the Remiel line and closes "seven names of archangels." The first copy has the closing words but no Remiel, so it counts seven while naming six; the second copy supplies the seventh. Charles's angle brackets here mean only that the Ethiopic has no parallel. The verse number 20:8 follows his edition.

a: I traveled on to a place where nothing had been made.
p: The Ge'ez text used here has nothing for this verse.

readings.orig: Καὶ ἐφώδευσα ἕως τῆς ἀκατασκευάστου (Kai ephōdeusa heōs tēs akataskeuastou)
readings.en: And I traveled as far as the unformed place
readings.plain: I traveled on to a place where nothing had been made.

readings.en: (no words for this verse)

why: The Plain English Translation translates the Greek, which both Gizeh copies have. "Unformed" (akataskeuastos) is the word the Greek Old Testament uses in Genesis 1:2 for the earth before creation, and 21:2 describes such a place.

a: These are some of the stars
p: The EOTC text says "these are angels."

readings.orig: እሉ ውእቶሙ እምነ ከዋክብት (ʾəlu wəʾtomu ʾəmnä käwakbət)
readings.en: these are some of the stars
readings.plain: These are some of the stars

readings.orig: οὗτοί εἰσιν τῶν ἀστέρων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ (houtoi eisin tōn asterōn tou ouranou)
readings.en: these are some of the stars of heaven
readings.plain: These are some of the stars

readings.w: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church printed text (EOTC)
readings.orig: እሉ እሙንቱ መላእክት (ʾəlu ʾəmuntu mälaʾkət)
readings.en: these are angels
readings.plain: These are angels

why: The Plain English Translation follows Dillmann and both Greek copies. The EOTC reading says what the stars stand for (see 18:14–16; 86:1), but the verse itself speaks of stars.

a: four hollow places
p: The Greek says hollow; the Ge'ez says beautiful.

readings.orig: τέσσαρες τόποι ἐν αὐτῷ κοῖλοι (tessares topoi en autō koiloi)
readings.en: four hollow places in it
readings.plain: four hollow places

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible reads the same, with small spelling differences
readings.orig: ወ፬መካናት ሠናያት (wä[4]mäkanat śänayat)
readings.en: and four beautiful places
readings.plain: four beautiful places

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. Koiloi, "hollow," and kaloi, "beautiful," look alike, and the rest of the verse describes deep, dark pits. The same choice is made in 22:3.

a: These hollow places
p: As in 22:2.

readings.orig: Οὗτοι οἱ τόποι οἱ κοῖλοι (Houtoi hoi topoi hoi koiloi)
readings.en: these hollow places
readings.plain: These hollow places

readings.orig: እላ መካናት ሠናያት (ʾəla mäkanat śänayat)
readings.en: these beautiful places
readings.plain: These beautiful places

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek, as in 22:2.

a: Their souls will not be killed
p: The Ge'ez says the souls will not be killed; the Greek says they will not be punished.

readings.orig: ወነፍሶሙሰ ኢትትቀተል (wänäfsomusä ʾittəqätäl)
readings.en: but their souls will not be killed
readings.plain: Their souls will not be killed

readings.orig: τὰ δὲ πνεύματα αὐτῶν οὐ τιμωρηθήσονται (ta de pneumata autōn ou timōrēthēsontai)
readings.en: but their spirits will not be punished
readings.plain: Their spirits will not be punished

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez. Either way the point is that this group stays where it is and is not raised for judgment. The Greek also has a line, which Charles judged added, saying they suffer less because they were afflicted on earth.

a: The trees were not like one another.
t: Not alike, or like nut trees?
p: The Greek says the trees were like nut trees.

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible reads the same, with small spelling differences
readings.orig: ወዕፀወኒ ኢይትማሰሉ (wäʿḍäwäni ʾiytəmasälu)
readings.en: and the trees were not alike
readings.plain: The trees were not like one another.

readings.orig: καὶ τὰ δένδρα αὐτῶν ὅμοια καρύαις (kai ta dendra autōn homoia karyais)
readings.en: and their trees were like nut trees
readings.plain: The trees were like nut trees.

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez, the base text, but the Greek may well be older: most of these verses compare the trees to known ones (30:2; 32:4), and Charles took it to mean almond trees.

a: Look! He has come with ten thousands of holy ones
p: The Ge'ez, the Greek and Jude word God's coming and his army a little differently.

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible reads the same, with small spelling differences
readings.orig: ወናሁ መጽአ በትእልፈት ቅዱሳን (wänahu mäṣʾä bätʾəlfät qədusan)
readings.en: and behold, he came with myriads of holy ones
readings.plain: Look! He has come with ten thousands of holy ones

readings.orig: ὅτι ἔρχεται σὺν τοῖς μυριάσιν [αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῖς] ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ (hoti erchetai syn tais myriasin [autou kai tois] hagiois autou)
readings.en: for he comes with his myriads [and his] holy ones
readings.plain: For he comes with his holy ten thousands

readings.orig: Ἰδοὺ ἦλθεν κύριος ἐν ἁγίαις μυριάσιν αὐτοῦ (Idou ēlthen kyrios en hagiais myriasin autou)
readings.en: look, the Lord came with his holy myriads
readings.plain: Look! The Lord has come with his holy ten thousands

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez. Its "look" and past tense "has come" agree with Jude against the Gizeh Greek's "for he comes." Charles marks "his … and" in the Greek as a corrupt addition (square brackets), which leaves "with his holy myriads," as in Jude. Only Jude has "the Lord": in 1 Enoch God himself comes (1:3–4). The Aramaic of 4Q204 survives only in a few letters here and does not decide the wording.

a: on all
p: The Greek and Jude say "against all"; the Ge'ez says "on them."

readings.orig: ποιῆσαι κρίσιν κατὰ πάντων (poiēsai krisin kata pantōn)
readings.en: to execute judgment against all
readings.plain: on all

readings.orig: ποιῆσαι κρίσιν κατὰ πάντων (poiēsai krisin kata pantōn)
readings.en: to execute judgment against all
readings.plain: on all

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible reads the same, with small spelling differences
readings.orig: ፍትሐ ላዕሌሆሙ (fətḥä laʿlehomu)
readings.en: judgment on them
readings.plain: on them

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Gizeh Greek, which Jude 15 matches word for word. "On them" in the Ge'ez narrows the judgment to the wicked just named; "on all" fits 1:7, where judgment comes on everyone.

a: of all their wicked deeds that they have done, and of the harsh words they have spoken, and of everything that wicked sinners have said against him
p: The Gizeh Greek, the Aramaic as reported, and Jude all have the harsh words. The Ge'ez lacks them.

readings.orig: περὶ πάντων ἔργων ⟨τῆς ἀσεβείας⟩ αὐτῶν ὧν ἠσέβησαν ⟨καὶ σκληρῶν ὧν ἐλάλησαν λόγων καὶ περὶ πάντων ὧν κατελάλησαν⟩ κατ’ αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀσεβεῖς (peri pantōn ergōn tēs asebeias autōn hōn ēsebēsan kai sklērōn hōn elalēsan logōn kai peri pantōn hōn katelalēsan kat’ autou hamartōloi asebeis)
readings.en: concerning all their deeds of ungodliness which they have done ungodly, and the hard words which they have spoken, and concerning all that ungodly sinners have spoken against him
readings.plain: of all their wicked deeds that they have done, and of the harsh words they have spoken, and of everything that wicked sinners have said against him

readings.w: Aramaic, 4Q204 (as reported by Mazich from Milik's reading)
readings.orig: רברבן וקשין (rabrevan uqashin)
readings.en: [… words] great and hard […]
readings.plain: of all their wicked deeds that they have done, and of the proud and harsh words they have spoken, and of everything that wicked sinners have said against him

readings.orig: περὶ πάντων τῶν ἔργων ἀσεβείας αὐτῶν ὧν ἠσέβησαν καὶ περὶ πάντων τῶν σκληρῶν ὧν ἐλάλησαν κατ’ αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἀσεβεῖς (peri pantōn tōn ergōn asebeias autōn hōn ēsebēsan kai peri pantōn tōn sklērōn hōn elalēsan kat’ autou hamartōloi asebeis)
readings.en: for all their deeds of ungodliness which they have done ungodly, and for all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against him
readings.plain: of all their godless deeds that they have done, and of all the harsh things that godless sinners have spoken against him

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible reads the same, with small spelling differences
readings.orig: በእንተ ኲሉ ዘገብሩ ወረሰዩ ላዕሌሁ ኃጥአን ወረሲዓን (bäʾnətä kʷilu zägäbru wäräsäyu laʿlehu ḫaṭʾän wäräsiʿan)
readings.en: concerning all that the sinners and the godless have done and committed against him
readings.plain: of everything that the sinners and the wicked have done and committed against him

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Gizeh Greek. In Charles's edition the words in angle brackets are in the manuscript but have no parallel in the Ethiopic; they are not his additions. The Aramaic of 4Q204, as Milik read it (reported by Mazich; not checked here against Milik's plates), keeps "great and hard," so the two oldest witnesses agree against the Ge'ez. The Ge'ez translator or an early copyist most likely skipped from one "concerning all" to the next. Jude 15 is a shortened form of the same Greek.

a: deep and wide and very smooth
p: The Greek adds that three hollows were dark and one bright, with a spring.

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible reads the same, with small spelling differences
readings.orig: ዕሙቅ ወርኂብ ወልሙጽ ጥቀ (ʿəmuq wärḫib wälmuṣ ṭəqä)
readings.en: deep and wide and very smooth
readings.plain: deep and wide and very smooth

readings.orig: βάθος (καὶ πλάτος) ἔχοντες καὶ λίαν λεῖοι, ⟨τρεῖς αὐτῶν σκοτεινοί, καὶ εἷς φωτεινός, καὶ πηγὴ ὕδατος ἀνὰ μέσον αὐτοῦ. καὶ εἶπον·⟩ (bathos kai platos echontes kai lian leioi, treis autōn skoteinoi, kai heis phōteinos, kai pēgē hydatos ana meson autou. kai eipon)
readings.en: having depth and breadth and very smooth; three of them dark and one bright, and a spring of water in its midst. And I said:
readings.plain: deep and wide and very smooth. Three of them were dark and one was bright, with a spring of water in the middle of it. I said,

why: The Plain English Translation keeps the Ge'ez, the base text, but the Greek line may well be original: a copyist could skip it, and it matches the bright spring for the righteous in 22:9 and the "three" of 22:9. It is in the Gizeh manuscript, not a supplement of Charles.

a: He lifted me up
p: The Greek says one of the holy ones came and raised him.

readings.orig: ወአንሥአኒ (wäʾänśəʾäni)
readings.en: and he lifted me up
readings.plain: He lifted me up

readings.orig: ⟨καὶ προσελθών μοι εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἤγειρέν με⟩ καὶ ἔστησέν με (kai proselthōn moi heis tōn hagiōn ēgeiren me kai estēsen me)
readings.en: and one of the holy ones came to me and raised me, and he stood me up
readings.plain: One of the holy ones came to me and raised me. He stood me up

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez, the base text, in which the Lord himself lifts Enoch. The Greek line about one of the holy ones has no Ethiopic parallel; it may be original, and it fits the many angels around the throne (14:22–23).

a: and no trees were planted on them
p: The Greek says no trees grew in the valleys; the Ge'ez says trees were planted.

readings.orig: καὶ δένδρον ⟨οὐκ⟩ ἐφυτεύετο ἐπ’ αὐτάς (kai dendron ouk ephyteueto ep’ autas)
readings.en: and no tree was planted on them
readings.plain: and no trees were planted on them

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851); the Ethiopian church's Bible reads the same, with small spelling differences
readings.orig: ወዕፅ ይተከል በላዕሌሆሙ (wäʿḍ yətäkäl bälaʿlehomu)
readings.en: and trees are planted on them
readings.plain: and trees were planted on them

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Greek. In 27:1 Enoch asks why the land is full of trees while the valley is cursed, which fits bare valleys. The Ge'ez lacks the negative, perhaps by a slip.

a: the vision of the Holy One
t: "The vision of the Holy One" or "a holy vision"?
p: The EOTC text and the Greek have "the Holy One"; Dillmann has "a holy vision."

readings.w: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church printed text (EOTC)
readings.en: the vision of the Holy One
readings.plain: the vision of the Holy One

readings.orig: τὴν ὅρασιν τοῦ ἁγίου (tēn horasin tou hagiou)
readings.en: the vision of the Holy One
readings.plain: the vision of the Holy One

readings.orig: ራእየ ቅዱሰ (raʾyä qədusä)
readings.en: a holy vision
readings.plain: a holy vision

why: The Plain English Translation follows the EOTC text and the Greek, which agree. Dillmann's form is an adjective ("holy"); the EOTC's is a noun in construct ("of the Holy One"). The title fits 1:3, where "the Holy Great One" comes out.

a: Semyaza, who was their leader, Urakib, Rameel, Kokabel, Tamiel, Ramuel, Danel, Ezeqeel, Baraqel, Azazel, Armaros, Batrael, Ananel, Zaqebe, Samsaweel, Sartael, Turel, Yomyael and Arazyal
p: Every witness spells the names differently, and the counts differ: 19, 21, 20.

readings.w: Dillmann's Ge'ez text (1851), with spellings matched to 8:1–3; the Ethiopian church's Bible spells several names differently (for example Uraki, Baramel, Ananel)
readings.orig: ስምያዛ ዘውእቱ መልአኮሙ ኡራኪበራሜኤል አኪበኤል ጣሚኤል ራሙኤል ዳንኤል ኤዜቄኤል ሰራቁያል አሳኤል አርምርስ በጥረአል አናንኢ ዘቄቤ ሰምሳዌኤል ሰርተኤል ጡርኤል ዮምያኤል አራዝያል (səmyaza zäwʾətu mälʾäkomu ʾurakibärameʾel ʾäkibäʾel ṭamiʾel ramuʾel danʾel ʾezeqeʾel säraquyal ʾäsaʾel ʾärmərs bäṭräʾäl ʾänanʾi zäqebe sämsaweʾel särtäʾel ṭurʾel yomyaʾel ʾärazyal)
readings.en: Semyaza, who is their leader, Urakibarameel, Akibeel, Tamiel, Ramuel, Danel, Ezeqeel, Saraquyal, Asael, Armers, Batrael, Ananʾi, Zaqebe, Samsaweel, Sartael, Turel, Yomyael, Arazyal (19)
readings.plain: Semyaza, who was their leader, Urakib, Rameel, Kokabel, Tamiel, Ramuel, Danel, Ezeqeel, Baraqel, Azazel, Armaros, Batrael, Ananel, Zaqebe, Samsaweel, Sartael, Turel, Yomyael and Arazyal

readings.orig: Σεμιαζᾶ(ς)—οὗτος ἦν ἄρχων αὐτῶν—, Ἀραθάκ, Κιμβρᾶ, Σαμμανή, Δανειήλ, Ἀρεαρῶς, Σεμιήλ, Ἰωμειήλ, Χωχαριήλ, Ἐζεκιήλ, Βατριήλ, Σαθιήλ, Ἀτριήλ, Ταμιήλ, Βαρακιήλ, Ἀνανθνᾶ, Θωνιήλ, Ῥαμιήλ, Ἀσεάλ, Ῥακειήλ, Τουριήλ
readings.en: Semiazas (he was their leader), Arathak, Kimbra, Sammane, Daneiel, Arearos, Semiel, Iomeiel, Chochariel, Ezekiel, Batriel, Sathiel, Atriel, Tamiel, Barakiel, Ananthna, Thoniel, Rhamiel, Aseal, Rhakeiel, Touriel (21)
readings.plain: Semyaza, who was their leader, Arathak, Kimbra, Sammane, Daneiel, Arearos, Semiel, Iomeiel, Chochariel, Ezekiel, Batriel, Sathiel, Atriel, Tamiel, Barakiel, Ananthna, Thoniel, Rhamiel, Aseal, Rhakeiel and Touriel

readings.w: Greek quoted by George Syncellus, about AD 810
readings.orig: αʹ Σεμιαζᾶς ὁ ἄρχων αὐτῶν. βʹ Ἀταρκούφ. γʹ Ἀρακιήλ. δʹ Χωβαβιήλ. εʹ Ὁραμμαμή. ϛʹ Ῥαμιήλ. ζʹ Σαμψίχ. ηʹ Ζακιήλ. θʹ Βαλκιήλ. ιʹ Ἀζαλζήλ. ιαʹ Φαρμαρός. ιβʹ Ἀμαριήλ. ιγʹ Ἀναγημάς. ιδʹ Θαυσαήλ. ιεʹ Σαμιήλ. ιϛʹ Σαρινᾶς. ιζʹ Εὐμιήλ. ιηʹ Τυριήλ. ιθʹ Ἰουμιήλ. κʹ Σαριήλ
readings.en: 1 Semiazas their leader, 2 Atarkouph, 3 Arakiel, 4 Chobabiel, 5 Horammame, 6 Rhamiel, 7 Sampsich, 8 Zakiel, 9 Balkiel, 10 Azalzel, 11 Pharmaros, 12 Amariel, 13 Anagemas, 14 Thausael, 15 Samiel, 16 Sarinas, 17 Eumiel, 18 Tyriel, 19 Ioumiel, 20 Sariel (20)
readings.plain: 1 Semyaza their leader, 2 Atarkouph, 3 Arakiel, 4 Chobabiel, 5 Horammame, 6 Rhamiel, 7 Sampsich, 8 Zakiel, 9 Balkiel, 10 Azalzel, 11 Pharmaros, 12 Amariel, 13 Anagemas, 14 Thausael, 15 Samiel, 16 Sarinas, 17 Eumiel, 18 Tyriel, 19 Ioumiel, 20 Sariel

why: The Plain English Translation keeps the Ge'ez list, the base text, but spells four names the way 8:1–3 spells the same angels, so a reader can follow them: Akibeel is printed Kokabel (Greek Chochariel, compare 8:3 Chochiel), Saraquyal is Baraqel (Greek Barakiel), Asael is Azazel (Greek Aseal, Syncellus Azalzel "the tenth"), and Armers is Armaros (Greek Arearos). Charles made the same identifications. Ge'ez "Urakibarameel" is printed as two names, Urakib and Rameel, as most translators do; Ananʾi is printed Ananel. The Aramaic forms in 4Q201–202 are fragmentary and are not given here.

a: The sinners will curse you continually
t: Cursing you, or cursing by you
p: The Greek says those who curse will curse by you; the Ge'ez says sinners will curse you.

readings.orig: ወኪያክሙ ይረግሙ ኃጥኣን ዘልፈ (wäkiyakmu yərägmu ḫaṭʾan zälfä)
readings.en: and you the sinners will curse continually
readings.plain: The sinners will curse you continually

readings.orig: καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν καταράσονται πάντες οἱ καταρώμενοι (kai en hymin katarasontai pantes hoi katarōmenoi)
readings.en: and by you all who curse will curse
readings.plain: All who curse will curse by your names

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez here. The Greek fits Isaiah 65:15 (a name used in curses), the passage the verse is built on, and may be older.

a: and it will be the same for you as for the sinners
p: The Gizeh Greek has several extra lines of blessing for the chosen here.

readings.orig: ወለክሙ ኅቡረ ምስለ ኃጥኣን (wäläkmu ḫəburä məslä ḫaṭʾan)
readings.en: and for you, together with the sinners
readings.plain: and it will be the same for you as for the sinners

readings.orig: καὶ πάντες οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ [καὶ ἀσεβεῖς ἐν ὑμῖν ὀμοῦνται. καὶ πάντες οἱ (ἀν)αμάρτητοι χαρήσονται, καὶ ἔσται αὐτοῖς λύσις ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ πᾶν ἔλεος καὶ εἰρήνη καὶ ἐπιείκεια· ἔσται αὐτοῖς σωτηρία, φῶς ἀγαθόν …] (kai pantes hoi hamartōloi kai asebeis en hymin omountai. kai pantes hoi anamartētoi charēsontai, kai estai autois lysis hamartiōn kai pan eleos kai eirēnē kai epieikeia; estai autois sōtēria, phōs agathon …)
readings.en: and all the sinners [and godless will swear by you. And all the sinless will rejoice, and they will have release from sins and every mercy and peace and kindness; they will have salvation, a good light …]
readings.plain: and all the sinners and the wicked will swear by you. All who are without sin will rejoice. They will have forgiveness of sins, every mercy, peace and kindness. They will have salvation, a good light

why: The Plain English Translation follows the Ge'ez. The Greek addition, which runs into 5:7 and 5:8, is in the manuscript but Charles judged it a corrupt expansion (square brackets): it repeats the blessings of 5:7–8 in other words. Some translations made from the Greek print part of it.
